title: Temporal Animation Conductor
description: The user conducts a mystical animation stage where CesiumMan performs choreographed movements around the Nemetona temple, while ShaderBall2 orbs act as energy nodes that control animation speed, direction, and blending. Users must arrange orbs along a timeline rail, assign animation properties, couple multiple inputs to achieve synchronized performances, and use undo/redo to refine their composition while respecting an energy conservation system.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Temporal Animation Conductor. Load nemetona.glb centered at origin as a stage backdrop, CesiumMan.glb with its skeletal animation placed in front, and three instances of ShaderBall2.glb as draggable energy orbs. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,8) looking at origin with OrbitControls. Lighting: warm DirectionalLight plus ambient, with colored point lights on each orb. Core system: A horizontal timeline rail (visible line from x=-4 to x=4 at y=0.2, z=3) where orbs can be dragged and snapped to positions. Each orb controls a parameter: Red orb controls playback speed (0.1x-3x based on x-position), Blue orb controls animation time offset (scrub through CesiumMan animation), Green orb controls a vertical bounce amplitude added to CesiumMan's root. Energy Conservation Law: total energy equals 10 units. Speed costs energy proportional to its value, bounce amplitude costs 2 per unit, and time-offset precision costs 1 per snap point used. Display remaining energy in a HUD. If energy is exceeded, the last change is rejected and reverted. Multi-input coupling: holding Shift while dragging any orb makes all three orbs move proportionally, redistributing their parameters simultaneously. Interactions: (1) click to select an orb (highlight it), (2-4) drag each of three orbs to timeline positions, (5-7) fine-tune each orb with mouse wheel for sub-position adjustment, (8) Shift-drag for coupled movement, (9-10) press Z for undo and Y for redo (maintain a 20-step history stack storing all orb positions and parameter states). Display a bottom panel showing current Speed, Offset, Bounce values and energy remaining. CesiumMan's AnimationMixer should update every frame reflecting current orb parameters. Add subtle particle trails between orbs and CesiumMan using Points geometry to visualize energy flow. All interactions use raycasting for orb selection and dragging on the timeline plane.
